w: What's tested Sertoli cells versus Leydig cells (he said this is where he would study) How a male body is built before birth (AMH, testosterone, DHT) and the two disorders where it goes wrong How sperm are made and matured How testosterone is made and what turns it into DHT or estrogen How the brain and pituitary control the testes, and how to read LH, FSH and testosterone What each gland adds to semen Which nerves run erection and ejaculation, and how sildenafil works The 4 G's Genetic sex is XY or XX. Gonadal sex is testes or ovaries. Genital sex is a penis or a vagina. Gender is identity. The first three are built in order, and each needs the one before it. The disorders in this lecture are where the layers don't match. The male system has three jobs: make sperm, sexual performance, and run sex traits through hormones. Building a male: three signals AMH from Sertoli cells removes the Müllerian ducts. No uterus. He called this an important piece to remember. Testosterone from Leydig cells (driven by hCG from the placenta, and LH) builds the inside male parts from the Wolffian ducts: epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles. DHT, made from testosterone by 5-alpha-reductase, builds the penis, scrotum and prostate. No signals means female. Female is the default. Two disorders Androgen insensitivity: the androgen receptor is broken or missing (often X-linked). XY, testes, but they stay inside and never drop. AMH works, so no uterus or ovaries. Testosterone can't act, so no inside male parts. Female outside, with a blind-ended vagina. Female puberty: breasts, little body hair. 5-alpha-reductase deficiency: no DHT. XY, testes, no uterus, inside male parts present (testosterone works), female outside. Often raised as girls. At puberty testosterone rises, body hair and muscle appear, and that is often when it's found. Same in both: XY, testes, no uterus (AMH still works), female outside. Trick: can testosterone act? Androgen insensitivity, no. 5-alpha-reductase deficiency, yes. Inside the testis Sperm are made in the walls of the coiled seminiferous tubules. The youngest cells sit at the wall; as they mature they move to the middle. The epididymis stores sperm, and the vas deferens carries them to the urethra. Leydig cells sit between the tubules. Sertoli cells (the nurse cells, run by FSH). He said comparing them with Leydig cells is where he would study. Wrap around and feed the sperm. Tight junctions make the blood-testis barrier. The testis is immune-privileged: immune cells kept out can't attack the sperm. Secrete fluid that moves sperm along. Secrete androgen-binding protein, which keeps testosterone high inside the tubules. Spermiation: strip extra cytoplasm and release the sperm. Make inhibin and aromatase, eat defective sperm, and make AMH in the fetus. Leydig cells (run by LH) make testosterone from cholesterol. That's their main job: worth remembering. Stay cool Sperm are made best at 34 degrees Celsius, he said, a few degrees below body temperature. (The histology lecture says about 35. Same idea.) That is why the testes hang outside the body. When warm, the testes drop away from the body to cool (he tied this to the cremaster). When cold, the dartos tightens the scrotum and pulls them closer. Arteries and veins twist together, and heat moves from artery to vein, so the blood is cooler when it arrives. Making sperm Spermatogonia sit at the tubule wall and keep dividing by mitosis. Some become spermatocytes. Meiosis happens here: primary spermatocyte, first division, secondary spermatocytes, second division, spermatids. One spermatocyte makes four spermatids, each with 23 chromosomes (22 plus an X or a Y). Sertoli cells strip the extra cytoplasm, and spermatids become sperm. His slide: about two months. (The histology lecture gives about 74 days for the whole process.) Sperm leaving the testis can't swim yet. In the epididymis, after 18 to 24 hours, they start to gain the power to swim and fertilize. They are stored there for months. Sperm parts: head (DNA), acrosome (from the Golgi, enzymes to get through the egg's layers), a midpiece full of mitochondria for energy, and a whip-like tail. Testosterone and its enzymes A steroid, made from cholesterol in Leydig cells when LH tells them to. LH turns up the first step, cholesterol desmolase (side-chain cleavage), just as ACTH does in the adrenal. Leydig cells can also turn the weak adrenal androgens into testosterone. Some tissues answer to testosterone. Others answer more to DHT and carry a lot of 5-alpha-reductase. 5-alpha-reductase: testosterone to DHT. Aromatase: testosterone to estradiol, androstenedione to estrone. FSH turns it up. It is mostly in the Sertoli cells, from before birth on. His slide says Leydig cells from puberty; he told the class to cross that out. Men need a little estradiol: it goes to the blood for other tissues, and back to the Leydig cells to help them build protein. The control loop Hypothalamus makes GnRH, in pulses. Pituitary makes LH and FSH. LH to Leydig: testosterone. FSH to Sertoli: sperm. Testosterone shuts down GnRH (hypothalamus) and LH (pituitary). Inhibin (from Sertoli) shuts down FSH, at the pituitary only. It doesn't act on the hypothalamus. Steady, non-stop GnRH lowers LH and testosterone. Pulses are needed. When testosterone drops, GnRH and LH go up to bring it back. When it climbs, they go down. That keeps testosterone in a narrow range. Memory hook: L for LH, L for Leydig. S for Sertoli, S for sperm (FSH). Reading the labs Testes failing: testosterone low, LH and FSH high. Pituitary failing: all three low. Injected testosterone: testosterone high, LH and FSH low, few sperm. The testis loses its own high testosterone and its FSH. FSH high by itself: low inhibin from damaged tubules. Testosterone over a lifetime: high before birth, a bump just after birth, quiet in childhood, up at puberty, steady (not monthly) in adults, down in old age (late-onset hypogonadism). What goes into semen Seminal vesicles: most of the fluid, 60 to 70 percent (his slide: 50 to 80). Fructose for energy. Prostaglandins make the female tract contract, which helps sperm along. Fibrinogen makes the semen clot, which holds sperm in the female tract. Prostate: 20 to 30 percent. Thin, milky fluid with citrate, phosphate and calcium. Neutralizes acid. Makes PSA, an enzyme that breaks the clot down later so sperm can move on. Bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands: mucus before ejaculation. Lubricates and neutralizes the urethra. Point and shoot Point (erection) and lubrication: parasympathetic. Shoot (emission and ejaculation): sympathetic. Erection: nerves release acetylcholine and nitric oxide. NO opens the cavernosal arteries. It turns on guanylate cyclase, cGMP rises, smooth muscle relaxes, blood rushes into the spongy tissue, and the swollen tissue squeezes the veins shut. Sperm route: tubules, then epididymis, then vas deferens (sympathetic), then urethra. Sildenafil PDE5 breaks cGMP down. Sildenafil (Viagra) blocks PDE5, so cGMP lasts longer. It does nothing on its own: with no arousal, there is no nitric oxide and no cGMP to save. Quick hooks Point and shoot: parasympathetic points, sympathetic shoots. AMH removes, testosterone builds inside, DHT builds outside. Inhibin inhibits FSH, at the pituitary. Testosterone stops GnRH and LH. Aromatase: Sertoli cells. This lecture's numbers: 34 degrees, 4 spermatids, 23 chromosomes, 2 months. Seminal vesicles: most volume, sugar, the clot. Prostate: milky, PSA breaks the clot. Cowper's: slippery mucus first.
